text.p: Italian debt markets made a half-hearted bid for the upside by the end of trade but volumes were low and dealers said clients were not convinced.
"The market hasn't really got any direction. We're still losing on the spread over Germany," said one trader in London.

The November 2006 Btp spread over Germany crept out one basis point from Tuesday to stand at 163. The Btp itself ended nine basis points up at 104.72 and was yielding 7.19 percent. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 10 basis points up at 110.67.
On futures, the March LIFFE contract was 29 basis points up at 131.11, having veered past 130.00 support to 130.85 earlier.
On the charts, the future had support at 131.00, then 130.80, while resistance set up camp at 131.50/60.

Dealers said uncertainty remained in the market over who was going to be in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), with plenty of uncertainty hanging over Italy. "When there is such uncertainty traders buy core bonds like Treasuries and Bunds. That's why we're losing on the spread," one said.
Sounding the EMU tattoo, Prime Minister Romano Prodi, speaking in parliament, expressed renewed optimism Italy would trim its 1997 budget deficit enough to join EMU from the start.
